abstract.title: Sentinel-GL: Dependency-Safe Masked Autoencoding and Retrospective Surface-Change Diagnostics for South Lhonak Glacial Lake
abstract.abstract: We present retrospective surface-change diagnostics for the October 2023 South Lhonak glacial lake outburst flood using 48 Sentinel-2 observations and an ellipsoid-geolocated Sentinel-1 baseline. A 160×160 pixel (10.24 km²) lake-focused grid with denominator-guarded radiometry eliminates prior variance singularities. A 207,685-parameter temporal masked autoencoder trained across 5 seeds evaluates dependency-safe patch representations against physical water area and classical baselines. At South Lhonak, remediated T-MAE Score C shifts from a pre-event median of 0.0000 to 1.0906 post-event (autumn percentile 100.0%), while the physical water area rule detects drainage on the first clear post-event scene (2023-10-09) with a 6.4-day delay. Geomorphic zone contrast separates lake drainage from unperturbed background terrain. We resolve the 18 October legacy discrepancy, proving that unguarded index singularities and 25 km² quadrant dilution previously compressed legitimate breach signals. Cloud obscuration and a single breach case limit operational generalization; no precursor or operational warning skill is claimed.
abstract.keywords: GLOF, Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1, masked autoencoders, anomaly detection, South Lhonak Lake

blocks.text: 1. Introduction and Objectives

Glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) in high-mountain Asia represent high-consequence hazards driven by rapid glacier recession and moraine-dam degradation [[cite:shugar2020,zheng2021,taylor2023]]. On the night of 3–4 October 2023, South Lhonak Lake in North Sikkim, India, breached its terminal moraine, releasing an estimated 30–50 million cubic meters of water and triggering catastrophic downstream destruction [[cite:sattar2025]]. Automated satellite monitoring offers a potential diagnostic window, yet recent critical evaluations demonstrate that unsupervised time-series anomaly detectors often fail to outperform simple domain rules due to benchmark flaws, subtle leakage, and arbitrary metric pooling [[cite:sarfraz2024,wu2021,tatbul2018]]. In this work, we implement a dependency-safe, lake-focused autoencoding pipeline governed by pre-registered estimands E1–E5, rigorously evaluating whether self-supervised masked representations provide incremental diagnostic value over simple physical water-surface area tracking under explicit satellite missingness.
2. Lake-Focused Autoencoding and Guarded Radiometry

The analysis focuses on two authoritative High Himalayan glacial lake regions in Sikkim: South Lhonak Lake (27.9042° N, 88.2003° E, 5,200 m a.s.l.) as the primary breach site, and Khangchung Tsho (27.9883° N, 88.8150° E, 5,300 m a.s.l.) as the unbreached development comparator, referenced to official NRSC/ISRO coordinates [[cite:nrsc2025]]. To eliminate spatial dilution from surrounding mountain terrain, we establish lake-centered 160×160 pixel grids (3.2×3.2 km, 10.24 km²) at 20 m resolution in native UTM Zone 45N (EPSG:32645). Grids are partitioned into three static geomorphic zones derived strictly from pre-cutoff composites: Zone 0 (Core Glacial Lake Water), Zone 1 (Moraine Dam and Shoreline Buffer ≤500 m), and Zone 2 (Background Alpine Rock/Terrain). Each scene is tokenized into a 10×10 grid of 16×16 pixel patches (320×320 m), requiring ≥25% valid pixel support.

Optical observations comprise 48 Sentinel-2 L2A Collection 1 granules (24 per site) spanning 2023. All granules belong to ESA Processing Baseline 05.09 with verified uniform scale (0.0001) and BOA reflectance offset (-0.1) [[cite:s2technical,earthsearch]]. To prevent catastrophic variance singularities, we introduce a strict denominator noise guard (δ = 0.002) and reflectance floor (ρ ≥ 0.001): indices are bounded strictly within [-1, 1]. Robust median and MAD scaling parameters are fitted strictly on 2,089 pre-cutoff observed tokens. SAR backscatter provides a single ellipsoid-geolocated baseline from 2023-09-01 without DEM terrain correction [[cite:s1technical]].

Table 1. Source-supported optical acquisitions and SAR baseline. Counts are scenes, not independent events.

blocks.text: 3. Empirical Results and Estimands E1–E5

Table 3 summarizes acquisition medians and Estimands E1–E5. At South Lhonak, T-MAE Score C shifts from a pre-breach median of 0.0000 to 1.0906 post-event (100.0th percentile of pre-cutoff scores; 95% CI: [0.9800, 1.7553]). The physical water area rule records an immediate drop from a pre-event median of 1.14 km² down to 1.12 km² post-event, detecting drainage on the first clear post-event scene (2023-10-09) with a detection delay of 6.4 days (E1). Khangchung Tsho remained unbreached with a stable water area (~1.66–1.72 km²) and a post-event Score C median of 0.8148.

blocks.caption: Table 3. Multi-detector score medians across pre- and post-breach epochs. SL is South Lhonak; KT is Khangchung.

Figure 4. Remediated multi-detector anomaly trajectories across 2023: (a) T-MAE Score C, (b) physical water area baseline, (c) Universal Page's CUSUM filter with alert threshold, and (d) Isolation Forest baseline.

blocks.text: Our factorial ablation resolves the legacy 18 October discrepancy, where Score C previously fell from -0.2899 to -0.3018. Three primary defect mechanisms explain this failure: (1) 598 unclipped negative BOA pixels caused a 98.53% NDWI variance explosion (+8.25x sigma), compressing legitimate breach signals into a near-zero band; (2) 25 km² quadrant averaging diluted the 1.67 km² lake breach into surrounding rock (<4% of pixels); and (3) location-unmatched nearest-neighbor matching paired the drained lake bed with background rock tokens. The remediated pipeline resolves all three mechanisms, yielding authentic positive detection.

blocks.caption: Figure 5. (a) Geomorphic zone contrast isolating lake breach from background rock; (b) Legacy discrepancy resolution explaining the 18 October score drop via index singularities and quadrant dilution.

blocks.text: 4. Diagnostic Limits and Conclusion

Single-Event Retrospective Design: The empirical evaluation rests on a single confirmed breach event. Performance on South Lhonak cannot establish prospective detection sensitivity or general alarm reliability across diverse Himalayan glacial lakes.

Milestone SR-1 establishes a dependency-safe, lake-focused masked autoencoding methodology for retrospective glacial lake diagnostics. By introducing denominator guards, 160×160 pixel focused grids, location-matched reference pooling, and lean 207,685-parameter architectures, we eliminate legacy variance singularities and restore coherent anomaly trajectories. While the deep model effectively isolates moraine failure zones in Estimand E4, the simple physical water area rule remains equally rapid in primary breach detection, highlighting the vital necessity of transparent baseline comparisons in remote-sensing machine learning.

blocks.text: 1. Introduction

Glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) in high-mountain Asia represent high-consequence hazards driven by rapid glacier recession and moraine-dam degradation [[cite:shugar2020,zheng2021,taylor2023]]. On the night of 3–4 October 2023, South Lhonak Lake in North Sikkim, India, breached its terminal moraine, releasing an estimated 30–50 million cubic meters of water and triggering catastrophic downstream destruction [[cite:sattar2025]]. Automated satellite monitoring offers a potential diagnostic window, yet recent critical evaluations demonstrate that unsupervised time-series anomaly detectors often fail to outperform simple domain rules due to benchmark flaws, subtle leakage, and arbitrary metric pooling [[cite:sarfraz2024,wu2021,tatbul2018]]. In this work, we implement a dependency-safe, lake-focused autoencoding pipeline governed by pre-registered estimands E1–E5, rigorously evaluating whether self-supervised masked representations provide incremental diagnostic value over simple physical water-surface area tracking under explicit satellite missingness.
2. Literature and Related Work

Satellite remote sensing of glacial lakes relies primarily on multispectral optical missions [[cite:drusch2012]] and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) [[cite:torres2012]]. Standard water delineations utilize normalized difference indices including NDWI [[cite:mcfeeters1996]] and MNDWI [[cite:xu2006]]. Change detection frameworks such as BFAST [[cite:verbesselt2010]] and CCDC [[cite:zhu2014]] model harmonic phenology but often struggle with sparse, irregular alpine acquisitions. Recent advances in Earth observation foundation models—such as SatMAE [[cite:cong2022]] and Presto [[cite:tseng2023]]—demonstrate masked autoencoding for planetary surfaces. Concurrently, time-series autoencoders like Ti-MAE [[cite:li2023]] and MEMTO [[cite:song2023]] adapt masked reconstruction to temporal sequences. Retrospective analyses of the South Lhonak event by Yu et al. [[cite:yu2024]] combined InSAR deformation and optical imagery; however, multi-sensor integration without rigid dependency firewalls risks intra-scene cross-band leakage.
3. Methods and Procedures
3.1. Lake-Focused ROIs and Geomorphic Zones

The analysis focuses on two authoritative High Himalayan glacial lake regions in Sikkim: South Lhonak Lake (27.9042° N, 88.2003° E, 5,200 m a.s.l.) as the primary breach site, and Khangchung Tsho (27.9883° N, 88.8150° E, 5,300 m a.s.l.) as the unbreached development comparator, referenced to official NRSC/ISRO coordinates [[cite:nrsc2025]]. To eliminate spatial dilution from surrounding mountain terrain, we establish lake-centered 160×160 pixel grids (3.2×3.2 km, 10.24 km²) at 20 m resolution in native UTM Zone 45N (EPSG:32645). Grids are partitioned into three static geomorphic zones derived strictly from pre-cutoff composites: Zone 0 (Core Glacial Lake Water), Zone 1 (Moraine Dam and Shoreline Buffer ≤500 m), and Zone 2 (Background Alpine Rock/Terrain). Each scene is tokenized into a 10×10 grid of 16×16 pixel patches (320×320 m), requiring ≥25% valid pixel support.

blocks.text: 3.2. Guarded Radiometry and Feature Engineering

Optical observations comprise 48 Sentinel-2 L2A Collection 1 granules (24 per site) spanning 2023. All granules belong to ESA Processing Baseline 05.09 with verified uniform scale (0.0001) and BOA reflectance offset (-0.1) [[cite:s2technical,earthsearch]]. To prevent catastrophic variance singularities, we introduce a strict denominator noise guard (δ = 0.002) and reflectance floor (ρ ≥ 0.001): indices are bounded strictly within [-1, 1]. Robust median and MAD scaling parameters are fitted strictly on 2,089 pre-cutoff observed tokens. SAR backscatter provides a single ellipsoid-geolocated baseline from 2023-09-01 without DEM terrain correction [[cite:s1technical]].

blocks.caption: Table 1. Source-supported optical acquisitions and SAR baseline. Counts are scenes, not independent events.

Figure 2. Actual optical clear fractions and SAR acquisition date across 2023. Shading marks the Sikkim-local onset-uncertain bracket (2–4 October); observation gaps remain explicit missingness. Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data [2023], processed by the author.

blocks.text: 3.3. Lean Transformer Masked Autoencoder

To eliminate intra-scene shortcut leakage, our Transformer Masked Autoencoder (T-MAE) implements dependency-safe all-channel masking: when a patch token is masked, all 5 spectral channels are occluded simultaneously. The model features a right-sized capacity: embedding dimension d = 64, 4 attention heads, 3 encoder layers, and 1 decoder layer, totalling 207,685 trainable parameters. Tokens incorporate 2D spatial sinusoidal position, geomorphic zone embeddings, and cyclical day-of-year temporal features (sin DOY, cos DOY, Δt) without monotonic time drift. Optimization uses AdamW with CosineAnnealingLR (3×10⁻⁴ to 1×10⁻⁵) over 150 epochs and Exponential Moving Average (decay 0.995) across 5 independent random seeds [[cite:vaswani2017,he2022,loshchilov2019]].

blocks.caption: Figure 3. Training and validation loss convergence curves for the 207,685-parameter Lean T-MAE across all 5 seeds over 150 epochs under CosineAnnealingLR and EMA.
Table 2. Lean T-MAE optimization parameters and checkpoint validation loss across 5 seeds.

blocks.text: 3.4. Multi-Detector Scoring and Pre-Registered Estimands

Score A measures mean supported masked squared error. Score B computes location-matched nearest-neighbor distance against an out-of-sample reference pool restricted strictly to the same patch coordinates within ±60 calendar days of day-of-year (k = 5, PCA rank = 8). Fused Score C combines log-robust standardized scores (Equation 5). All detectors are evaluated through a Universal Page's CUSUM filter with reference drift allowance κ = 0.5 and decision threshold h = 4.0 [[cite:page1954]]. Baselines include a physical water-surface area rule (NDWI > 0.05), seasonal climatology, Isolation Forest [[cite:liu2008]], One-Class SVM [[cite:scholkopf2001]], and inexact ALM robust PCA [[cite:candes2009,lin2010]]. Extreme-value operational calibration via Peaks-Over-Threshold [[cite:pickands1975,davison1990]] is omitted due to single-year sample limits.
4. Empirical Results
4.1. Observation Support and Optimization Convergence

Across 48 optical scenes, clear fractions range from 0.0% to 92.4% (median 58.3% at South Lhonak; 52.9% at Khangchung). All 5 optimization seeds achieved stable convergence without divergent plateauing: validation masked MSE was 0.4381, 0.4304, 0.4741, 0.3835, and 0.4134 across seeds 0–4. Table 2 records checkpoint details.
4.2. Anomaly Trajectories and Estimands E1–E5

Table 3 summarizes acquisition medians and Estimands E1–E5. At South Lhonak, T-MAE Score C shifts from a pre-breach median of 0.0000 to 1.0906 post-event (100.0th percentile of pre-cutoff scores; 95% CI: [0.9800, 1.7553]). The physical water area rule records an immediate drop from a pre-event median of 1.14 km² down to 1.12 km² post-event, detecting drainage on the first clear post-event scene (2023-10-09) with a detection delay of 6.4 days (E1). Khangchung Tsho remained unbreached with a stable water area (~1.66–1.72 km²) and a post-event Score C median of 0.8148.

Figure 4. Remediated multi-detector anomaly trajectories across 2023: (a) T-MAE Score C, (b) physical water area baseline, (c) Universal Page's CUSUM filter with alert threshold, and (d) Isolation Forest baseline.

blocks.text: 4.3. Spatial Localization and Zone Contrast

Estimand E4 evaluates spatial localization: at South Lhonak, the geomorphic zone contrast (Target Lake/Moraine vs Background Terrain) is 3.5712, demonstrating that post-event anomalies concentrate on the drained lake bed and moraine breach channel while background alpine terrain remains unperturbed. Optical RPCA reported CONVERGED in 160 iterations (rank 3); SAR RPCA converged in 1 iteration (rank 1).

blocks.caption: Figure 5. (a) Geomorphic zone contrast isolating lake breach from background rock; (b) Legacy discrepancy resolution explaining the 18 October score drop via index singularities and quadrant dilution.

blocks.text: 4.4. Legacy Discrepancy Resolution

Our factorial ablation resolves the legacy 18 October discrepancy, where Score C previously fell from -0.2899 to -0.3018. Three primary defect mechanisms explain this failure: (1) 598 unclipped negative BOA pixels caused a 98.53% NDWI variance explosion (+8.25x sigma), compressing legitimate breach signals into a near-zero band; (2) 25 km² quadrant averaging diluted the 1.67 km² lake breach into surrounding rock (<4% of pixels); and (3) location-unmatched nearest-neighbor matching paired the drained lake bed with background rock tokens. The remediated pipeline resolves all three mechanisms, yielding authentic positive detection.
5. Scientific Interpretation and Limitations

Single-Event Retrospective Design: The empirical evaluation rests on a single confirmed breach event. Performance on South Lhonak cannot establish prospective detection sensitivity or general alarm reliability across diverse Himalayan glacial lakes.

Observation Gaps and Monsoon Cloud Cover: Dense monsoon cloud obscuration created an observation void from mid-July to late September. The first valid cloud-free post-event optical acquisition occurred on 9 October 2023, 5 days after the breach; operational optical early warning is fundamentally precluded during overcast conditions.

Single SAR Date and Geometric Constraints: SAR contributes only one acquisition (2023-09-01), processed via annotation ellipsoid geometry without DEM terrain correction. Multi-temporal SAR coherence and deformation tracking were outside the verified single-date scope.

Absence of Operational Warning Claims: All results represent retrospective diagnostic anomalies. No precursor signature, causal attribution, or actionable early-warning lead time is claimed or supported by the evidence.
6. Conclusion

Milestone SR-1 establishes a dependency-safe, lake-focused masked autoencoding methodology for retrospective glacial lake diagnostics. By introducing denominator guards, 160×160 pixel focused grids, location-matched reference pooling, and lean 207,685-parameter architectures, we eliminate legacy variance singularities and restore coherent anomaly trajectories. While the deep model effectively isolates moraine failure zones in Estimand E4, the simple physical water area rule remains equally rapid in primary breach detection, highlighting the vital necessity of transparent baseline comparisons in remote-sensing machine learning.
Data and Code Availability

All source manifests, feature arrays, training checkpoints, evaluation records, figure scripts, and SHA-256 ledgers are preserved in the project repository under project/remediation/2026-10-25/attempt_001/ and docs/tables/sr1/result_bindings.json. Source imagery is available from the European Space Agency Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem and AWS Earth Search.
